Republican Senator's Religious Test for Office Sparks Constitutionality Debate
item.description: Joe Scarborough, host of MS NOW, became visibly agitated during a live broadcast on Thursday after viewing a clip of Republican Senator Bernie Moreno making remarks about Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, a practicing Muslim. Moreno, campaigning in Ohio, stated that El-Sayed is 'unfit to serve because of his religious beliefs,' arguing that El-Sayed does not understand the concept that 'our rights come from God Almighty, that Jesus came here for our salvation.' Scarborough, a former Republican member of Congress and practicing Baptist, expressed shock at Moreno's comments, emphasizing that the First Amendment explicitly prohibits the establishment of a religion and guarantees religious freedom. He pointed out that the Constitution allows for individuals of any faith, including Muslims, to run for office, stating, 'You can be a Christian, a Jew, a Muslim, an agnostic, an atheist, a Hindu. That makes us Americans.' Scarborough criticized Moreno for what he described as

item.title: Newegg Offers $15 Discount on PlayStation Gift Card for GTA 6 Preorder
item.description: IGN commerce editor Chris Reed has identified a current deal at Newegg that allows customers to purchase a $100 PlayStation Store digital gift card for $85, saving $15 through the promo code GTWF2793. This offer, available today only, provides the best discount on PlayStation credit ahead of the November 19 launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. The Ultimate Edition of GTA 6, which includes exclusive vehicles, weapons, and apparel, can be purchased with the $100 credit. Reed notes that while the deal requires spending $250 upfront for a $290 credit (with a free $40 PlayStation gift card), the $85 deal on the $100 card is more accessible for those planning to spend the full amount on the game. The gift card code is delivered via email within an hour of purchase, and users can redeem it at the PlayStation Store to apply the credit toward the GTA 6 preorder. Reed emphasizes that physical copies of GTA 6 are not available in disc format, with all versions requiring digital downloads via a code. The

item.title: Obama addresses Cheesecake Factory controversy at Georgia rally, mocks Trump's White House decor
item.description: Former President Barack Obama recently addressed the Cheesecake Factory controversy at a 'United for Georgia' rally, where he elaborated on his viral comment comparing President Donald Trump's White House to a Cheesecake Factory. Obama clarified that while Trump was not bothered by the Saddam Hussein reference, he was deeply offended by the Cheesecake Factory mention, claiming the administration mobilized a 'whole of government response' to the joke rather than addressing economic issues like inflation. The former president also criticized Trump's White House decorating choices, noting the president was 'super gluing gold medallions to the mantle in the Oval Office' while the country faced significant challenges. Conservative commentators had previously accused Obama of elitism over the Cheesecake Factory line, with some claiming he 'has never been in a Cheesecake Factory.' However, Obama's latest remarks drew strong support from his allies, with former White House officials and politi

item.title: Francis Halzen Awarded Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for IceCube Neutrino Observatory Contributions
item.description: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced on October 6 that Belgian-American physicist and astrophysicist Francis Halzen has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. This marks the first unshared Physics Nobel since 1992 and the fifth in history related to neutrinos. Halzen's work bridges particle physics and astrophysics, focusing on the detection of neutrinos, often called 'ghost particles' due to their near-invisibility and ability to pass through matter without interaction. The article details the historical context of neutrino research, from Wolfgang Pauli's 1931 theoretical prediction to the 1956 experimental confirmation by Clyde Cowan and Frederick Reines. It highlights key milestones, including Raymond Davis Jr.'s 1968 detection of solar neutrinos and the 1987 Kamiokande II detection of neutrinos from supernova SN 1987A. Halzen's pivotal contri

item.title: Toronto Police Seek Elderly Man After Sexual Assault at School Open House
item.description: Toronto police have issued a public appeal for information regarding a sexual assault that occurred during a school open house event in Scarborough on Tuesday. The incident involved an underage victim who was allegedly assaulted on school grounds by a suspect who attended the open house. According to police reports, the victim managed to stop the assault before the suspect fled the scene on foot. The suspect is described as an elderly male with balding gray and white hair, a gray and white beard, and was last seen wearing a beige jacket, a blue and white plaid button-up shirt, black pants, and black shoes. Police have released a photograph of the suspect to aid in the investigation. The assault reportedly took place in the Guildwood Parkway and Livingston Road area. Authorities are urging anyone with information to contact investigators immediately. This incident has raised concerns about safety at community events, particularly those involving minors. item.title: Republicans express concern over Trump's campaign focus amid declining support
item.description: According to The Atlantic's Jonathan Lemire, Republicans are privately expressing concern that President Donald Trump's final campaign message to voters does not address the issues most important to their supporters. Trump's campaign strategy has reportedly centered on dismissing the affordability crisis, attacking comedian Bill Maher, and praising Senator Jon Husted's physical appearance. During a Michigan rally, Trump referred to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as a jihadist five times and spent approximately three and a half minutes discussing Husted's football career. At a Mississippi rally, he devoted roughly seven minutes to discussing White House redecorating. Many Republicans, including those within Trump's inner circle, have told Lemire that Trump has lost touch with his base, with his approval ratings falling to the low 30s. Candidates in competitive races, such as Susan Collins in Maine and John Sununu in New Hampshire, have reportedly requested that Trump avoid campaigning in their

item.title: Trump's Legacy of Controversy and Legal Troubles Shapes Midterm Election Narrative
item.description: The article, written by Ray Richmond, a journalist and adjunct professor, argues that the upcoming midterm elections will serve as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency and his ongoing legal and political controversies. The author presents a detailed list of Trump's legal issues, including 34 felony convictions, 4 criminal indictments, and 91 felony counts originally charged, alongside his business failures, such as six corporate bankruptcies. The piece also highlights Trump's impact on American institutions, including the erosion of trust in elections, the peaceful transfer of power, and the independence of the Justice Department. Richmond emphasizes that Trump's actions have led to a deterioration in basic civility, making it difficult to disagree with others without resorting to personal attacks. The article criticizes Trump for his role in undermining scientific expertise, public health institutions, and the educational system, as well as for elevating authoritarian figures lik

item.title: Daily Fiber Supplement Shows Promise in Reducing Knee Arthritis Pain and Enhancing Muscle Strength
item.description: A clinical trial led by researchers at the University of Nottingham has revealed that a daily prebiotic fiber supplement, specifically inulin, can significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis (OA) pain while improving muscle strength. The study, published in the journal Nutrients, involved 117 adults with knee OA who were assigned to one of four treatment groups: inulin alone, digital physical therapy exercises (PSE) alone, a combination of inulin and PSE, or a placebo. Participants taking inulin experienced notable pain reduction, improved grip strength, and decreased pain sensitivity compared to those in the physical therapy group. The supplement also demonstrated a much higher adherence rate, with only 3.6% dropout in the inulin group versus 21% in the physical therapy group. Inulin, a naturally occurring fiber found in foods like chicory root and Jerusalem artichokes, is not broken down by digestive enzymes but instead nourishes beneficial gut bacteria in the large intestine. item.title: Critical UEFI Firmware Flaw Affects Most Servers, Allows Pre-Boot Code Execution
item.description: A critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, has been discovered in the TianoCore EDK II open-source codebase used by most server vendors and data centers for UEFI firmware. The flaw, rated 9.5 out of 10 in severity, is a memory-corruption issue in the ICMP component that allows attackers to execute malicious code before the operating system and firmware defenses like Secure Boot activate. The vulnerability affects the PXE-Base Code driver (NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe), which handles network boot processes, enabling attackers to send malicious ICMP error messages that overwrite memory buffers. This can lead to code execution in ring 0, the most privileged CPU level, before security mechanisms like TPM and Secure Boot are engaged. The flaw has been present for 16 years and impacts systems that boot from network resources, including servers, storage equipment, and devices relying on EDK2-based firmware. While the vulnerability requires local network access for exploitation, it poses

item.title: Ukrainian Authorities Face Growing Scrutiny Over Forced Mobilization Practices
item.description: In Ukrainian cities, the routine checks of military registration documents and the forcible transfer of men to Territorial Recruitment Centers (TCCs) have become a common feature of wartime life. TCC personnel and police officers conduct vehicle stops, pedestrian inspections, and joint raids, often using physical force. Mobile teams frequently change locations, with residents warning each other through local Telegram groups. Social media and news outlets have documented cases of beatings, unlawful detentions, and denial of access to lawyers. The Ukrainian ombudsman has reported a significant increase in complaints about these practices, with some cases leading to criminal convictions. However, many convictions result in suspended sentences, allowing offenders to continue serving. The Council of Europe and United Nations have also raised concerns about violations of human rights, including excessive restrictions on conscientious objection. item.title: A Doctor's Unusual Examination and the Words That Left a Patient Shocked
item.description: A recent incident involving a medical examination has sparked discussion about patient-doctor communication and the importance of clear, respectful dialogue in healthcare settings. The patient, who wishes to remain anonymous, described an encounter with a physician who, during a routine gynecological exam, made comments that were both unexpected and unsettling. The doctor reportedly looked at the patient's genital area and then stated three words that the patient found shocking. While the exact words were not disclosed, the patient expressed concern about the appropriateness of the remarks and the lack of explanation provided. This incident highlights the need for healthcare providers to maintain professionalism and ensure that patients feel comfortable and informed during examinations. Medical ethics require that doctors communicate clearly with patients, explaining procedures and any observations made during exams. The patient's experience underscores the potential for misunderstandi

item.title: NME releases 2025-2026 coffee table book featuring 50 emerging artists with exclusive content
item.description: NME has launched 'NME The Cover 2025-2026', a 300-page hardcover coffee table book collecting 50 stories from its weekly franchise that champions emerging artists globally. The third edition in the annually released series features artists such as Maruja, Balu Brigada, Die Spitz, Gigi Perez, BOYNEXTDOOR, and many others, with bespoke artwork, interviews, and previously unseen photography. The book is available for purchase with a 20% launch discount, with orders beginning dispatch on November 6. Free UK delivery is offered, and international shipping is free on orders over £200. Karen Gwee, Managing Editor (Music) at NME Networks, emphasized the mission of breaking new and next music through The Cover, calling it a 'true labour of love.' The Cover relaunched in May 2023 with the goal of connecting emerging artists with NME's audience of millions of music fans. The book includes a full list of featured artists, with additional content available on Spotify and Apple Music. Previous editi

item.title: Sauna Bathing Temporarily Boosts Immune Cell Circulation, Study Finds
item.description: A recent study conducted by researchers in Finland has revealed that a single 30-minute sauna session, followed by a brief cold shower, triggers a temporary surge in white blood cells circulating in the bloodstream. The findings, published in the journal Temperature, indicate that sauna bathing mobilizes immune cells that typically reside in tissues, allowing them to move more freely throughout the body. This increased circulation enhances the body's ability to monitor for pathogens such as bacteria and viruses. The study measured various types of white blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, which are critical for immune responses. Neutrophils act as first responders to infections, while lymphocytes are involved in recognizing specific threats and producing antibodies. The increase in these cells was observed immediately after the sauna session but returned to baseline levels within 30 minutes. Researchers noted that the temporary rise in immune cell activity resembles the

item.title: Faith Domergue: A 1950s Horror and Sci-Fi Star Known for Her Dark Beauty
item.description: Faith Domergue (1924 or 1925–1999) was an American actress celebrated for her dark beauty and significant roles in 1950s science fiction and horror films. Discovered as a teenager by Howard Hughes, she was signed to a contract and groomed for stardom, though her early career faced delays and limited opportunities. Domergue gained lasting recognition in the mid-1950s with appearances in cult classics such as This Island Earth (1955), It Came from Beneath the Sea (1955), and Cult of the Cobra (1955), earning her a place among the era’s early 'scream queens.' Her striking features and intense screen presence made her a distinctive figure in mid-century genre cinema. These films, now considered classics, highlight her ability to captivate audiences with her dramatic presence. Domergue's work in these movies cemented her legacy as a memorable face of 1950s science fiction and film noir. Her career, though not as prolific as some contemporaries, remains influential in the history of genre fi

item.title: Samsung TV's Pet Care feature raises privacy concerns over data sharing with advertisers
item.description: In April 2025, Samsung introduced Vision AI sets with features called Pet Care and Family Care, which could detect dog barks or baby cries in an empty room and send alerts to owners' phones. The company stated these features only worked when the TV was turned off. However, on October 23, 2026, a reverse engineer known as log4j shared findings suggesting Samsung TVs send data about barks, cries, sensor readings, and camera streaming duration to Samsung servers. The researcher discovered this through unpatched security flaws that allowed full control of the TV, revealing sound-classification models, screen capture logs, and cross-device advertising IDs. Samsung's automatic content recognition (ACR) system, which samples screen content twice per second, has been documented for years, but the new claims involve potential audio data collection. The researcher alleges that even when ACR is turned off, data might still be transmitted. Samsung has disputed the claims, stating that viewing-reco

item.title: GOP Strategist Criticizes Ex-Trump Aide's Proposal to Cut Ukraine Funding to End War
item.description: On Wednesday's episode of CNN's 'NewsNight,' guest-hosted by Michael Smerconish, Republican strategist Shermichael Singleton engaged in a heated exchange with Caroline Sunshine, a former Trump White House aide, over her proposal to end the Ukraine-Russia conflict by cutting U.S. funding to Ukraine. Sunshine argued that the U.S. should withdraw financial support to force Ukraine to negotiate a peace deal, stating that Ukraine is not a NATO ally and the U.S. has no role in the war except to end it. Singleton strongly opposed the idea, calling it 'the most absurd thing' and accusing Sunshine of being 'incredibly naive.' He emphasized that Russia, not Ukraine, initiated the conflict, noting that 'it wasn't the Ukrainians. It was the Russians.' Singleton further criticized Sunshine for suggesting that Ukraine should be pressured to negotiate, arguing that the U.S. has never taken such a stance before. He questioned her understanding of the issues, stating, 'Do you even understand these issu

item.title: Vali Myers: Australian Artist and Spiritual Pioneer of Positano
item.description: Vali Myers, widely known as the 'Witch of Positano,' was an Australian artist, dancer, and mystic whose life spanned the post-war avant-garde scenes of Paris, New York's Chelsea Hotel, and a remote Italian canyon. Born in Sydney in 1930, Myers became a prominent figure in the Beatnik movement in Paris, where she was photographed by Ed van der Elsken for his book 'Love on the Left Bank.' She associated with cultural icons like Jean Cocteau, Allen Ginsberg, and Jean-Paul Sartre. After overcoming an opium addiction, Myers retreated with her partner Rudi Rappold to a cliffside ravine near Positano, Italy, where they lived in an abandoned stone structure without modern amenities. For decades, she immersed herself in nature, creating intricate pen-and-ink and watercolor drawings that depicted mystical themes, animal forms, and powerful representations of femininity. She also established a wildlife sanctuary for rescued animals, contributing to the area's protection as a WWF oasis. Myers main

item.title: Bluesky Blocks Links to DHS Employee Data Leak, Citing Safety Concerns
item.description: Bluesky has blocked links to a newly leaked archive containing records of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees and contractors, labeling the pages as 'malicious.' The files include personal contact information such as email addresses and phone numbers, shared without authorization, which violates Bluesky's community guidelines. The company chose to block the links rather than remove individual posts to avoid restricting public discussion or broader access to reporting on the leak. The DHS records, published by the transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), detail employee names, contact information, and internal group memberships, including those tied to surveillance and undercover operations. A WIRED investigation revealed the files provide insight into DHS organizational structure, from leadership to individual immigration agents, and who has access to certain technologies. item.title: Snow Peak Campfield: A Japanese-Inspired Retreat on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula
item.description: Snow Peak Campfield, located on Washington's Long Beach Peninsula, offers a unique blend of Japanese design and Pacific Northwest natural beauty. The campfield features Jyubako suites, small cabins made of pale pine and plywood, each approximately 200 square feet with a queen bed, futon, kitchenette, and private bathroom. Priced from $130 per night, these cabins are designed to encourage guests to stay connected with nature, with low furniture that positions the eye at the top edge of the glass door to the porch, gently nudging guests outside. The main attraction is the Ofuro, a Japanese-style bathhouse with a hot pool maintained at 104 degrees, a hinoki cypress sauna, cold plunge, and showers. The bathhouse is thoughtfully designed with angled beams echoing the surrounding trees and an open side facing a grove of alders at the edge of a pond. The Long Beach Peninsula, where the campfield is situated, is known for its wide sandy beaches, razor clamming, kite flying, and storm watching.

item.title: MUHC Researchers Identify New Vesicles Linked to Cancer Cell Migration and Metastasis
item.description: Researchers at McGill University Health Centre (MUHC) have identified a novel mechanism by which migrating cancer cells communicate and spread throughout the body. The study, led by Prof. Julia Burnier and PhD student Thupten Tsering, reveals that cancer cells release specialized structures called motile vesicles (MoVes), which carry genetic material including cancer-associated mutations. These vesicles, previously thought to be cellular waste, are now understood to play a critical role in cell-to-cell communication during cancer progression. The discovery emerged unexpectedly while investigating how cancer cells release DNA, leading to the identification of MoVes as a key component in the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process. EMT is a biological mechanism that allows cells to become more mobile and invasive, contributing to tumor progression and treatment resistance. The research team observed a significant increase in MoVes production when non-cancerous cells were induc

item.title: Early Voting by Black Voters Rises in Southern States Ahead of 2026 Midterms
item.description:
Early voting among Black Americans has increased significantly ahead of the 2026 midterm elections, particularly in Southern states where Republican redistricting efforts have targeted majority-Black congressional districts. According to The Bulwark, Black voters have cast more than 160,000 additional ballots compared with the same stage of the 2022 midterm elections, raising questions about whether Republican efforts to reshape electoral districts could have unintended political consequences.
The developments follow the Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais, a case that originated in Louisiana and weakened the protections provided by Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Following the decision, Republicans in several states moved to redraw congressional maps and dismantle majority-Black districts. Democrats had argued that these changes could motivate Black voters, including younger people and those who do not regularly participate in midterm elections, to become more politica

item.title: Trump Administration Challenges Court Order on Park Closure for Golf Course Renovation
item.description: The Trump administration's Justice Department has raised objections to a federal court order requiring detailed notice before closing East Potomac Park in Washington, D.C., for a golf course renovation. In a filing with the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, the department argued that the court's requirements for 'prompt notice' and extensive documentation, including naming every individual involved and assessing the impact on the park, are overly burdensome. The closure, scheduled for November 15, is part of a plan to replace the current public golf course with a 'World Class, championship-level golf course' designed by Tom Fazio, capable of hosting major tournaments like the U.S. Open and the Ryder Cup. The National Park Service has signed a new lease with National Links Trust, the company currently operating the East Potomac Golf Course, which will cease operations by the closure date but will continue managing Rock Creek and Langston golf courses. The administration

item.title: Dancing With the Stars Season 35 Features First Perfect Score and Double Elimination During Horror Movie-Themed Episode
item.description: Dancing With the Stars season 35 celebrated Halloween with a horror movie-themed episode, featuring performances inspired by films such as Saw, Black Swan, and Joker. The episode marked the first perfect score of the season when Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson earned a 40/40 for their contemporary dance to 'Toxic' by 2WEI, inspired by the horror film Saw. This performance placed them at the top of the leaderboard with a combined score of 76/80 after combining scores from both Horror Movie Night and Dedication Night. The episode also saw the elimination of two couples: Jackson Olson and Emma Slater, and Tyler Cameron and Sharna Burgess, who had the lowest combined scores. The elimination was determined by a combination of judges' scores and viewer votes from both Dedication and Horror Movie Night. item.title: Europe moves toward direct talks with Russia amid shifting geopolitical dynamics
item.description: After months of hesitation and internal debate, European leaders are signaling a decisive shift toward direct engagement with Russia to address the Ukraine conflict and reshape continental security architecture. Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre recently held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, marking a significant step in Europe's diplomatic approach. While lacking formal mandates, their initiative positioned Nordic leaders as key interlocutors, with the Kremlin confirming plans for continued direct communication. The European Commission and Council are preparing a joint delegation, led by Bjoern Seibert, to join upcoming talks in Abu Dhabi, aiming for a multilateral format involving Europeans, Ukrainians, Americans, and Russians—a departure from previous US-centric negotiations. item.title: Defense Secretary Hegseth removes Pentagon chief planner amid strategic uncertainty
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has removed Army Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, the Pentagon's chief planner, from his position on the Joint Chiefs of Staff without providing an explanation, according to The Atlantic. Sylvia, who led the Joint Staff's strategy, plans and policy directorate (J5), is the second person to be removed from that role within a year, following the forced retirement of his predecessor, Army Lt. Gen. Joseph McGee. The timing of the removal is particularly sensitive as President Donald Trump considers potential military action against Iran following next week's elections, with U.S. Central Command reportedly preparing strike options ranging from limited strikes on nuclear sites to broader economic pressure campaigns. A former Joint Chiefs of Staff official described the J5 role as a critical bridge between field troops, Pentagon policy, and the White House, suggesting that losing this position at this moment could be problematic. item.title: Measles Outbreak Spreads from South Carolina to Washington State in Multiple Incidents
item.description: The news article details multiple instances of measles transmission from South Carolina to Washington state within a two-week period. According to the report, there were five distinct importation events where individuals from South Carolina traveled to Washington state and subsequently spread the virus. In the first incident, South Carolina residents visited public places while infectious, leading to four residents with close contact falling ill. These four individuals then visited schools, healthcare facilities, and a church, causing nine additional cases among their contacts and one person exposed in a public location, totaling 14 cases from January 15 to February 17. The second incident involved two state residents returning from South Carolina who fell ill on January 15-16, but no additional cases were linked to them. item.title: Speaker Challenges Israel’s International Critics With a Biblical Appeal to Loyalty
item.description:
Israel’s international image becomes a question of biblical loyalty and political identity

The speaker argues that Israel should judge its standing in the world not primarily by how it is viewed abroad, but by how Israelis themselves assess the countries that criticise or oppose them. Addressing the question of Israel’s deteriorating image in Europe, Canada and the United States, the speaker shifts the discussion from diplomacy and international opinion to religious identity, moral authority and allegiance to the Jewish state.

The speaker’s identity cannot be established with certainty from the available statement alone. No name, official position, event or other identifying information is provided, so attributing the remarks to a particular Israeli politician, religious figure or commentator would be speculative.

item.title: Fed Chair Warsh Delays Rate Hike Until After Midterms, Economist Questions Timing
item.description: A prominent economist, Justin Wolfers, has expressed confusion over Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's decision to maintain current interest rates instead of implementing a rate hike that markets anticipate. In his Platypus Economics newsletter, Wolfers noted that the Fed's decision to hold rates steady on Wednesday appears to be a six-week delay of an expected move, with markets already pricing in an 80% chance of a hike at the December meeting. Wolfers argued that the Fed's preferred inflation measure remains at 3.4% year-over-year through August, while consumer prices rose 3.7% through September, indicating that the economy still requires monetary tightening. He criticized the Fed's rationale that 'monetary medicine' needs time to take effect, pointing out that September's rate increase was only six weeks old and that delaying further action risks making subsequent measures less effective. item.title: Former State Department staffer Britt McHenry speaks out after NBA game altercation led to job loss
item.description: Britt McHenry, a former press advisor for the State Department and a former ESPN host, has publicly addressed the incident at a Washington Wizards basketball game that resulted in her losing her position. In a video posted on X, McHenry explained that she threw her beer at a group of hecklers after one of them made a derogatory comment about her 'getting gang raped outside.' She stated that she was defending a woman she admires, model Winnie Harlow, who was targeted by the hecklers for her vitiligo. McHenry clarified that she and her friend Andrew, who flew in from Los Angeles, attended the game with tickets costing $250 to $300 each. The altercation began when a man in a 'knockoff Patagonia vest' criticized Milwaukee Bucks forward Kyle Kuzma, a former Wizards player, about his fiancée, Winnie Harlow, making comments about her skin condition. McHenry said the man made 'vile' remarks, prompting her to respond with a sarcastic comment about the man's girlfriend. This led to the man turni

item.title: Ken Paxton's campaign event draws sparse crowd amid mockery
item.description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate nominee, faced significant mockery after a campaign event in San Angelo drew only a small crowd, according to reports from the Daily Beast. The event, part of his 'Come and Take It Tour,' was held at the Arc Light Bar & Grill inside a Clarion Hotel. The venue typically offers a 4,000-square-foot ballroom for up to 300 people, but Paxton's team opted for a smaller 'Video Wall Room' that accommodates about 106 guests. The space was set up with only two rows of stadium chairs, and a Facebook video showed Paxton speaking for approximately 15 minutes. The Daily Beast reported that the campaign did not respond to inquiries about why the larger ballroom was not used. The sparsely attended event occurred the day after Paxton joined former President Donald Trump at two Texas rallies that drew much larger crowds. item.title: Trump's White House staff reports growing instability amid midterm election concerns
item.description: According to a New York Times report, President Donald Trump's behavior has become increasingly erratic behind closed doors, causing concern among those closest to him. The report, based on interviews with 16 current and former administration officials and Trump allies, reveals a sense of gloom descending on the White House less than a week before Election Day. Trump has been shrinking his circle of confidants, lashing out at critics, and dismissing polls showing his unpopularity. Many Republicans in competitive races are distancing themselves from the president, with some GOP advisers privately warning that his battleground rallies may harm rather than help their campaigns. Trump, however, remains determined to make the midterms a referendum on himself. The president has been spending more time with a small group of loyalists, including Natalie Harp, who has moved into the private dining room off the Oval Office, and Bill Pulte, the Federal Housing Finance Agency Director, who regular

item.title: Pentagon Inspector General Declines to Investigate Starlink Service Disruptions in Ukraine
item.description: A bipartisan group of nine U.S. senators, comprising four Republicans and five Democrats, has been denied a request to investigate the throttling of Elon Musk's Starlink satellite internet service in Ukraine. The Defense Department's inspector general (IG) declined the lawmakers' inquiry, stating that the Air Force is better equipped to address concerns regarding the slowdown. The senators sought the probe after Ukrainian officials reported that connection speeds on both Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, had been reduced, hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones. A congressional aide, speaking anonymously, characterized the IG's decision as a refusal to examine Musk and Starlink's role, despite the office's capability to do so. The aide noted that congressional concerns about Musk's control over Starlink have persisted for years, contributing to the development of Starshield. item.title: 1960 Aloha Week Parade in Honolulu Captured in Vibrant Kodachrome Photos
item.description: The 1960 Aloha Week Parade in Honolulu, Hawaii, is vividly captured through a series of vintage Kodachrome photographs, offering a nostalgic glimpse into mid-century Hawaiian culture and traditions. Established in 1946 to celebrate Hawaiian heritage, Aloha Week featured a vibrant array of cultural elements including colorful floral floats, pāʻū riders in traditional attire, marching bands, and the Royal Court parading through Waikiki's streets. The Kodachrome film's rich, saturated colors beautifully preserved the tropical flowers, bright costumes, and festive atmosphere of the event, providing a detailed visual record of the parade's pageantry. Among the images are specific scenes such as a Chinese-themed float with members of a Lion Dance organization, the Bridge of Friendship, Civic Club displays, debutantes from Kaimuki JCC, and the King and Queen of Aloha Week, Henry Rosa and Barbara Kukaua. item.title: Stripe Billing Coordination Design Prevents Duplicate Payment Attempts
item.description: Stripe Billing has a built-in feature called Smart Retries that automatically handles failed subscription payments by retrying at optimal times based on network and issuer signals. However, when merchants add a recovery layer on top of Stripe's system, a coordination problem arises: two systems may attempt to retry the same failed payment, leading to duplicated attempts, wasted resources, and potential double-charging. The Swipe Again team, which provides a recovery solution for Stripe Billing merchants, has developed a coordination design that integrates with Stripe's native retry system rather than competing with it. Their approach reads Stripe's current state before each retry decision, using observable invoice data such as attempt_count, next_payment_attempt, and decline codes. item.description: According to leading political analysts, four Republican incumbents may have significantly impacted their party's chances of maintaining control of the House of Representatives. The Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan ratings group, has quietly adjusted the rankings of four Republican lawmakers' races from 'toss up' to 'leaning Democrat' just weeks before the November 3 election. This change reduces the number of toss-up races from 21 to 17, lowering the Republicans' prospects of retaining House control. item.description: Lisa Guerrero, a former ABC 'Monday Night Football' sideline reporter, expressed shock and hurt after Michele Tafoya, a Republican Senate nominee backed by Donald Trump, dismissed her miscarriage on a 2023 podcast. Tafoya, who had worked alongside Guerrero on the same sports broadcast team, questioned the severity of Guerrero's miscarriage and labeled her a 'drama queen' during the podcast episode. item.description: The pro-MAGA podcast 'The Charlie Kirk Show' descended into chaos during a segment where former Republican strategist Tim Miller challenged the hosts' claims about President Donald Trump's record. The complaint states that Dollar General repeatedly mislabeled prices, failed to correct discrepancies despite knowing about the issue, and extracted millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges from vulnerable shoppers. The lawsuit, filed on September 11 in U.S. District Court, argues that the federal government has supremacy over state regulations under the Constitution's supremacy clause. The federal government claims that the state's actions violate constitutional principles by attempting to directly regulate federal agencies without congressional authorization. LaKeith Stanfield, who was previously announced as a star, has exited the project, and director Rob Savage has departed due to scheduling conflicts. The survey, commissioned by a Republican group, shows Democrat Amy Acton leading by eight points, up from a two-point lead she had before the ad began circulating on October 19. A separate Suffolk University poll also indicated a four-point gap, narrower than the nine-point lead shown in late September. item.title: Nanotyrannus Skeleton Fetches $47.3 Million at New York Auction, Sparking Scientific Debate
item.description: The mounted skeleton of a newly identified dinosaur, nicknamed Jodi, has sold at auction for $47.3 million, making it the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold. The 10-foot-tall skeleton, initially mistaken for a juvenile Tyrannosaurus rex, was confirmed by researchers to belong to a distinct genus, Nanotyrannus, in October 2023. The auction, conducted by Sotheby's in New York, saw intense bidding among six parties over a 12-minute period. The sale has reignited discussions within the scientific community about the ethics of private fossil sales versus public display. Sotheby's described Jodi as an 'excellent exhibition-ready' skeleton with 191 fossil elements and a nearly complete skull, noting it is one of only three such skeletons known to science. The skeleton was discovered in Montana's Hell Creek Formation by rancher Jodi Pierson and later excavated by commercial paleontologist Clayton Phipps, who also discovered the famous 'Dueling Dinosaurs' fossil. item.description: The Justice Department is laying the groundwork for potential new Espionage Act charges against former President Donald Trump by filing a criminal information in a case against former FBI Director James Comey, according to legal experts. The filing, made on October 5, 2026, just before the 10-year deadline for Espionage Act prosecutions expired, aims to establish a legal precedent that could help prosecutors bypass the need for a grand jury in future cases involving Trump. item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published draft guidance aimed at streamlining approvals for individualized gene therapies, a move welcomed by rare disease advocates who have long criticized the agency's previous approach. Under the current system, companies must submit separate drug approval applications for each patient's customized gene therapy, even when using fundamentally the same method to target different genes. This process has been deemed prohibitively expensive by advocates, who argue it creates unnecessary regulatory burdens. The new draft guidance formalizes a 'plausible mechanism pathway,' offering clearer rules for licensing and updating gene editing treatments. The radar boasts a 155-mile (250-kilometer) detection range for air targets and 31 miles (50 kilometers) for surface targets. Built on the Sea Giraffe AMB family, the new system integrates active electronically scanned array (AESA) technology with a software-defined architecture, enabling rapid beam steering and multi-tasking capabilities. This allows the radar to monitor multiple areas simultaneously while providing timely threat information. The system incorporates electronic counter-countermeasures (ECCM) to resist jamming attempts by adversaries, a critical feature in modern electronic warfare environments. Saab emphasizes the radar's modular design, which supports integration with other naval systems and allows for continuous software upgrades without requiring hardware replacement. item.title: Susan Saint James: Early Career and Iconic 1960s Television Roles
item.description: Emmy-winning actress Susan Saint James passed away on October 26, 2026, at the age of 80 after battling pancreatic cancer. item.title: Mary Trump warns of Trump administration's efforts to undermine midterm election integrity
item.description: Mary Trump, the niece of former President Donald Trump, has issued a stark warning about her uncle's alleged plan to manipulate the upcoming midterm elections. In her Substack newsletter titled 'SCAM: Donald's Plan to Rig the Midterms,' she describes the situation as a 'five alarm fire' and emphasizes that this election represents the most critical in modern history. Trump argues that the Trump administration is using federal institutions to investigate voter eligibility and challenge ballots, rather than focusing on legitimate election security concerns. She cites a Department of Homeland Security program that reportedly tasked untrained staff with reviewing 40 voter applications daily, and a Justice Department lawsuit targeting over 20,000 voters in California who were flagged as potential non-citizens. item.title: Vance's donor network under scrutiny in Brazil corruption probe
item.description: Vice President JD Vance has become the center of a Brazilian police investigation regarding whether his co-founded donor network, the Rockbridge Network, illegally supported Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign. Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the investigation following Bolsonaro's loss in the October 25 runoff election to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The investigation focuses on whether Rockbridge, which Vance co-founded in 2019, provided foreign financial assistance to Bolsonaro's campaign, which is illegal under Brazilian law. Dino's 38-page order directs federal police to examine communications between Rockbridge representatives and Brazilian businessmen Tallis Gomes and Pedro Sang, who are alleged to have facilitated financial support for Bolsonaro's campaign. The order also requires police to determine if the funding was linked to foreign interests in Brazil's rare earths and critical minerals, which are government-controlled resources. Bo

item.title: CBS's '60 Minutes' struggles with declining ratings amid revamped format
item.description: CBS's '60 Minutes' has experienced a significant ratings decline in its latest episode, drawing only 5.64 million total viewers and 558,000 viewers in the 25-54 demographic, according to Nielsen figures obtained by Status' Oliver Darcy. This performance marks a notable drop from historical averages, as the sixth episode of a '60 Minutes' season has not drawn fewer than 7 million total viewers or 1 million in the key demographic since 2000. The show, which underwent a major overhaul under CBS News chief Bari Weiss, is now facing criticism for failing to improve its performance, with 'America's Funniest Home Videos' and 'The Price Is Right' outperforming it in the crucial 25-54 demographic. A veteran TV executive noted that the show's previous hosts, such as Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega, were well-regarded, and the current direction has reportedly made the show 'worse' in the eyes of viewers. Despite the early season, the trend suggests a growing challenge for the revamped program, wi

item.title: Fox News viewership declines amid shifting political interests
item.description: Fox News is experiencing a significant drop in viewership, with October 2026 marking the network's lowest-rated month since December 2023, according to media newsletter Status. The decline is particularly pronounced among the 25-54 age demographic, which advertisers prioritize, with Fox News averaging just 98,000 viewers in this group—a 32% drop from the previous year. This represents the lowest-rated month for this demographic in 25 years. While Fox News still leads cable news overall, beating ESPN in total day viewership despite the return of football, the ratings decline is notable given the political context of the upcoming 2026 midterms. Weekday prime time shows hosted by Sean Hannity and Laura Ingraham are also seeing their lowest-rated months in both total viewers and the 25-54 demo since December 2023. "Fox & Friends," Trump's favored morning show, is struggling as well, with October 2026 marking its lowest-rated month in over 11 years. The network has begun declining to air Tr

item.title: Supreme Court Conservatives Push to Overturn Landmark Religious Freedom Ruling
item.description: The Supreme Court's conservative majority appears poised to potentially overturn a landmark 1990 ruling that has shaped religious freedom cases for decades. According to a CNN analysis cited in the article, the Court may deliver a significant victory for religious conservatives by revisiting Employment Division v. Smith, a decision written by the late Justice Antonin Scalia. The case in question, St. Mary Parish v. Roy, involves Catholic preschools and the Archdiocese of Denver seeking to participate in Colorado's universal preschool program without signing the state's nondiscrimination agreement covering sexual orientation and gender identity. A federal appeals court had previously ruled in favor of Colorado, relying on the Smith precedent which holds that neutral laws applicable to all do not require a 'compelling interest' to justify them. The Catholic groups are now urging the Court to overturn Smith entirely. The irony is noted as Scalia, who authored the Smith decision, was a con

item.title: Jennifer Lopez Announces New Single 'Proof of Love' Amidst Vinyl Reissue of 2011 Album 'Love?'
item.description: Jennifer Lopez is preparing to release her new single 'Proof of Love,' which will serve as a bonus track on the first-ever vinyl edition of her 2011 album 'Love?,' set for release in November. The singer revealed that the song was inspired by the emotional transition her life underwent when her twins, Max and Emme Muniz, left for college. Lopez described the song as a 'happy dance song' that also addresses 'pain and grief when someone's gone,' emphasizing that the song aims to transform grief into a positive marker of love. She shared that the experience of her children leaving home prompted her to return to the studio, resulting in what she considers some of her best work to date. The 'Love?' vinyl reissue, which includes three different versions available for pre-order starting October 28, coincides with the premiere of her new concert film 'The JLo Show: Live in Vegas,' airing on CBS and Paramount+ on Thanksgiving night, November 26. Lopez also mentioned that 'Proof of Love' will be

item.title: Matthew Perry's Family and Friends Share His Struggles with Addiction in Netflix Documentary
item.description: The Washington Post reports on a new three-part Netflix documentary featuring Matthew Perry, the late 'Friends' star, which delves into his personal life and career struggles. The documentary, titled 'Matthew Perry: The Documentary,' includes interviews with Perry's close friends and family members who share intimate details about his battles with substance abuse throughout his adult life. The film begins with archival footage of Perry in his early 20s, struggling financially while waiting for his breakthrough role as Chandler Bing on 'Friends.' In one of the old interviews featured in the documentary, Perry reflects on his early days, saying, 'I haven't prayed often, but I made a prayer and I said, God, you can do anything you want to me, just please make me famous.' The documentary provides a candid look at Perry's journey from his early career to his later years, highlighting both his professional successes and personal challenges. It offers viewers a deeper understanding of the act

item.title: Trump's Louisiana Data Center Payment Claim Debunked by Local News Investigation
item.description: President Donald Trump made a false claim during a recent interview, stating that every resident living near a Louisiana data center received a $10,000 check. The claim was debunked by WWL-TV, a local New Orleans news station, which investigated the matter and found no evidence of such payments. Trump's statement was made during an interview with Fox2 Detroit's Roop Raj, where he referenced a community in Louisiana that supposedly received $10,000 payments, leading to widespread support for the data center project. However, Louisiana Economic Development, the state agency responsible for economic development projects, confirmed they were unaware of any direct payments to residents. Spokesperson Emma Wagner stated, 'If there were $10,000 payments, I'd be shouting it from the rooftops.' item.title: Historian Mark Bray returns to U.S. after fleeing death threats, releases book on antifa targeting
item.description: Mark Bray, a historian and Rutgers University professor, has returned to the United States after being forced to flee with his family due to death threats and doxxing by far-right activists. The threats intensified after Bray's book 'Antifa: The Antifascist Handbook' was targeted by conservative groups, particularly Turning Point USA, which pushed for his dismissal. Bray's new book, 'Unpunctuated Death Threats,' set for release in January, details his experience of being labeled as part of a terrorist organization despite antifa being a decentralized movement against fascism, white supremacy, and racism. Bray criticized the right's narrative that portrays antifa as a top-down, organized entity funded by George Soros, calling it a recurring tactic that dates back to the Occupy Wall Street era. item.title: Former Intelligence Analyst Warns of Impending Crisis as Government Preparations Intensify
item.description: A former Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) staffer, Farijah 'Doc' St. Clair, has issued a stark warning to Americans about an impending crisis, urging immediate preparation. St. Clair, who now leads technology and intelligence at Crisis24, a risk firm owned by GardaWorld, shared his concerns on social media platform X, stating that 'your window to prepare, even with the basics, is closing.' He emphasized that governments signaling the need for citizen preparedness indicates that preparations have already been made for national leadership. St. Clair cited European governments advising citizens to stockpile supplies and Pentagon directives requiring U.S. military bases to sustain operations for 90 days as significant indicators of the severity of the situation. He described a potential scenario where major cities could face food shortages within three days due to supply chain failures, leading to looting and social unrest. St. Clair advised individuals to prepare quietly, avoiding visibl

item.title: SoFi Technologies Reports Strong Third Quarter 2026 Performance with $1.4 Billion in Revenue and $241 Million Net Income
item.description: SoFi Technologies, Inc. (SOFI) has reported its third quarter 2026 financial results, showcasing a record net revenue of $1.4 billion and net income of $241 million. The company's performance reflects significant growth across multiple business segments, with fee-based revenue reaching $1.429 billion for the quarter, up from $1.101 billion in the same period of 2025. Key drivers of this growth include strong performance in loan origination fees, technology services, and the newly launched SoFi Crypto platform. The company's loan origination fees increased to $607.6 million in Q3 2026 compared to $327.8 million in Q3 2025, while technology services revenue rose to $263.6 million from $151.7 million. The SoFi Crypto platform, launched in Q4 2025, contributed $3.7 million in net crypto transaction revenue during the quarter. SoFi's regulatory capital metrics also demonstrated strength, with CET1 risk-based capital at $9.52 billion, representing a 16.9% ratio against risk-weighted assets.

item.title: Democrats Adopt GOP Rhetoric to Oppose Transgender Sports Measure in Washington
item.description: Democrats in Washington state have successfully turned the Republican strategy against them regarding a ballot measure targeting transgender athletes. The proposed measure, which would require students to obtain health care provider verification of their sex to participate in girls' sports, has been countered by Democrats who frame it as government overreach rather than focusing on transgender athletes. This approach has united the party's progressive and moderate wings, with figures like Rep. Pramila Jayapal and Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez both opposing the measure. Jayapal emphasized using conservative values against them by highlighting the intrusion of government into family decisions. The opposition group No Hate in Washington State avoids using the term 'transgender' in ads, instead showing girls waiting for sex verification exams. Even the measure's supporters acknowledge the strategy is effective, with spokesperson Hallie Herzberg noting people questioning the need for genital

item.title: GOP Consultant Identifies 'Red Scream' as Key Threat to Senate Majority in Upcoming Midterms
item.description: A veteran Republican consultant, Alex Castellanos, has introduced the term 'Red Scream' to describe growing frustration among conservatives and independents who feel ignored by Donald Trump and Republican leaders ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. According to an Axios report cited in the article, this frustration could lead to lower voter turnout among these groups, potentially costing Republicans control of the Senate. Castellanos emphasized that the 'Red Scream' represents a more significant concern than the anticipated 'blue wave' of Democratic voter enthusiasm. Senate Republicans are currently assessing their prospects in several key states, with Iowa appearing to favor them, Ohio showing signs of slipping, and Alaska and Kansas viewed with increasing pessimism. The report notes that top Republican operatives struggle to envision a Senate majority beyond 51 seats. item.title: Democrats Target Trump's MAHA Coalition as Internal Disputes Threaten Midterm Support
item.description: Democrats are capitalizing on reported fractures within President Donald Trump's 'Make America Healthy Again' (MAHA) coalition, which has been a key component of his political base. The coalition, initially formed around promises to improve food safety and reduce harmful chemicals in the food supply, has faced internal disputes over the pace of policy changes, particularly regarding pesticide regulations. According to Axios, Trump's health adviser Calley Means resigned amid disagreements over the slow progress of food-policy reforms, with other MAHA leaders publicly criticizing the administration's handling of these issues. Vani Hari, known as Food Babe, accused Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. of being hindered by 'corporate capture and special interests' at the White House. item.title: TikTok Creators Monetize Copper Wire Stripping as a Side Hustle Amid Rising Prices
item.description: Copper prices have reached record highs, driving a surge in TikTok content where creators demonstrate stripping copper wire for resale. The trend, which has gained traction among diverse users including hobbyists, electricians, and teenagers, involves documenting the process of removing insulation from copper wire to sell the metal. According to the article, copper prices hit $14,473 per metric ton in September 2026, more than double the 2020 price, making scrap copper highly valuable. While some creators earn modest income from selling stripped copper, many generate significant revenue through TikTok Shop by promoting wire strippers and other tools. For example, one creator reported earning $1,446 from a video with 6.8 million views, while another sold over 20,000 wire strippers globally. The article notes that while copper theft has increased during price spikes, legal scrapers often work in teams, sharing profits and supporting each other, especially among those facing economic hard

item.title: The Institute of Housing and the Skin of Madrid: A Historical Reflection on Urban Development
item.description: The article discusses the historical context of housing policies in Spain, particularly under the Franco regime, and their lasting impact on urban development. It references the Instituto Nacional de la Vivienda (National Housing Institute) and its role in shaping residential areas, especially in Madrid. The author, Juan Manuel Grijalvo, explores how housing projects during Franco's era were designed to create a sense of stability and control, often displacing rural populations into urban outskirts. The text includes personal anecdotes from readers about living in neighborhoods built during this period, such as Colmenar Viejo, which were initially seen as undesirable but later became valuable due to their location. The discussion also touches on the political implications of housing policies, comparing the current state of public housing in areas governed by different political parties, such as PSOE and PP. item.title: GOP Claims Hidden Advantage in Senate Races Amid Democratic Missteps
item.description: The National Republican Senatorial Committee (NRSC) has been promoting a 'hidden advantage' for Republicans in the 2026 Senate races, claiming Democrats have made a 'huge mistake' by focusing too much on Texas while neglecting other traditionally Democratic states. In a fundraising email sent to donors, the NRSC criticized 'the Democrat media' for publishing polls showing Republican losses in Texas and accused outlets of 'gushing' over Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico's fundraising success. The email asserted that Republicans are 'SURGING in historically blue states!' and cited Minnesota as an example, claiming that Senate nominee Michele Tafoya is 'statistically TIED' with her Democratic opponent, though no specific poll was referenced. Hours later, former President Donald Trump amplified this message on Truth Social, endorsing Tafoya and warning that the only way she could lose is if Democrats 'cheat' by manipulating ballots. item.title: U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency Confirms China's Reusable Spaceplane in Satellite Image
item.description: The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that a satellite image circulating since 2024 depicts China's secretive reusable orbital spaceplane, resolving earlier uncertainty about its identity. The image, originally captured by Maxar Technologies (now Vantor), was first publicly shown in 2024 by U.S. Space Force Col. John Patrick during the Open Space Forum in South Korea. The DIA's 2026 report, 'Challenges to Security in Space 2026,' includes a higher-resolution version of the photograph, providing one of the clearest public views of China's experimental spacecraft. The report explicitly identifies the object as a Chinese spaceplane, noting its similarities to the American X-37B, an uncrewed reusable orbital vehicle operated by the U.S. Space Force. Both spacecraft feature compact shuttle-like fuselages, short wings, and twin vertical tails, though the Chinese vehicle appears to have longer wing chords. item.title: Egyptian court orders closure of independent news outlet Mada Masr and fines editor-in-chief
item.description: An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of Egypt's last remaining independent news outlets, and imposed a fine of three million Egyptian pounds ($53,400) on its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, for operating an unlicensed website. The New Cairo Misdemeanour Court also ordered the confiscation of the outlet's equipment and devices. Attalah was taken into custody following the ruling but was released hours later after Mada Masr paid the full fine. During her release procedures, Attalah learned she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison on charges of publishing false news and running an unlicensed website. Mada Masr's editorial criticized the court's actions, stating it entered court 'with a measure of faith in the law and the justice system' but found 'none of that faith intact.' item.title: Trump Banishes Bill Maher After Dinner Criticism, Echoes Soup Nazi Analogy
item.description: The article discusses a recent incident involving former U.S. President Donald Trump and comedian Bill Maher following a White House dinner. After Maher criticized Trump's low midterm approval ratings and mocked his behavior on his HBO show, Trump responded with a 1,300-word Truth Social post banning Maher from future dinners. The piece draws parallels between Trump's behavior and the 'Soup Nazi' character from Seinfeld, emphasizing Trump's demand for absolute loyalty at his dinners. The article notes that Maher was the second high-profile guest to face consequences for criticizing Trump, following former FBI Director James Comey, who was indicted multiple times after a 2017 dinner where Trump sought a loyalty pledge. The author argues that Trump's dinners function as a political echo chamber, inviting only those who offer unwavering support, such as Kanye West (Ye), Nick Fuentes, Kid Rock, and Stephen A. Smith. item.title: 1940s Brussels Street Life Captured in Vintage Photographs
item.description: The article presents a collection of 30 vintage photographs capturing everyday street life in Brussels during the 1940s. These images document pedestrians, shoppers, workers, and residents navigating the city's streets and squares throughout a decade marked by World War II occupation and postwar recovery. The photographs include specific locations such as Boulevard Adolphe Max and Boulevard Anspach, with dates ranging from March 1941 to October 1947. The images provide a historical record of urban life during the German occupation period (1940-1944) and the subsequent post-liberation era (1945-1947). The photographs show the subdued atmosphere of wartime Brussels alongside the renewed energy of the postwar period, offering a nostalgic glimpse into the city's daily movements and urban landscape more than eighty years ago. item.title: Women Athletes Face Higher Risk of Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S) with Subtle Early Symptoms
item.description: The article discusses Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (RED-S), a condition that occurs when athletes do not consume enough calories to meet the demands of their training or basic physiological needs. Women are at significantly higher risk than men, with a 2026 study in the Journal of Science and Medicine in Sport finding that 70% of high-level female athletes were at risk of developing RED-S. The condition can lead to a range of symptoms including fatigue, impaired concentration, frequent illnesses, poor recovery, irregular periods, weakened immune systems, and increased risk of injuries such as stress fractures. Early signs include persistent fatigue, longer recovery times after workouts, declining performance, more frequent illnesses, poor sleep, increased hunger, mood swings, hair loss, and weight loss. More serious symptoms include irregular or absent periods and frequent injuries. The article emphasizes that RED-S is not just about undereating but reflects chronic underfueling

item.title: Jio Platforms' stock surges 21% in debut following record-breaking Indian IPO
item.description: Jio Platforms, the Indian telecom and digital services unit owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani and backed by Meta and Google, experienced a 21% surge in its stock price during its market debut on Wednesday. The company raised $3.2 billion through India's largest and most subscribed initial public offering (IPO), which attracted over $77 billion in investor bids. The shares opened at ₹1,358 (approximately $14) per share, up from the IPO price of ₹1,119 ($12), valuing Jio Platforms at around ₹12.5 trillion ($131.9 billion). This makes it India's second-most valuable listed company after its parent Reliance Industries, which is valued at approximately ₹16 trillion ($168.6 billion). The IPO, which ran from October 21 to 22, saw bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer, with over 13.8 million applications, marking a record for the most subscribed stock offering in India. item.title: Cowboys End Two-Game Slide with Road Victory Over Eagles to Stay in NFC East Contention
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys secured a crucial 38-21 road victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night, ending a two-game losing streak and keeping pace with the 4-2-1 New York Giants in the NFC East. Quarterback Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes, including two to CeeDee Lamb and one to George Pickens, while running back Javonte Williams rushed for a career-high 155 yards, scoring the game-sealing touchdown with 2:21 remaining. The Cowboys' offense, which had struggled in recent games with only 29 combined points in their last two outings, showed significant improvement, marking the first time since 1983 that they achieved over 200 yards rushing and passing in a single game against the Eagles. Defensively, the Cowboys limited the Eagles' offense after allowing early touchdowns, recording one interception by DeMarvion Overshown and two sacks by Quinnen Williams and Donovan Ezeiruaku. item.title: Thunderbird: A Concept Space Station Designed Without Traditional Floors
item.description: The Thunderbird expandable space station, designed by OMI (Of My Imagination) in collaboration with Florida-based startup Max Space, represents a groundbreaking approach to space station architecture. Unlike traditional space stations that rely on gravity-defined floors, Thunderbird's interior design eliminates the concept of 'up' and 'down,' creating a circular layout where every surface can function as a floor. The station, which can be launched on a single SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, unfolds in orbit to approximately twenty times its folded size, providing 350 cubic meters of pressurized space—roughly a third of the International Space Station's volume. Its soft architecture, composed of layered fabric including Kevlar, meets or exceeds NASA safety standards for heat, vacuum, vibration, and micrometeoroid impacts. item.title: Federal Judge Rules LA's Top Prosecutor Unlawfully Serving, Bars Him from Two Cases
item.description: A federal judge has ruled that Bill Essayli, Los Angeles' top federal prosecutor, is unlawfully serving in his position and has barred him from overseeing two criminal cases. Senior U.S. District Judge J. Michael Seabright determined that the Justice Department had unlawfully delegated powers to Essayli, effectively making him a 'de facto' United States Attorney without proper Senate confirmation. The judge's ruling rejects the Justice Department's attempt to maintain Essayli's authority through a revised delegation of powers, stating that the revised arrangement made no meaningful difference as the powers in question could not have been lawfully delegated to him. Essayli, a former Republican California Assembly member, has been a key legal enforcer for the Trump administration, pursuing charges against protesters and activists while dropping cases involving administration allies. item.title: Jimmy Kimmel Encourages Protesters to Continue Chanting Ballroom Insult at Trump Events
item.description: Late-night host Jimmy Kimmel has encouraged hecklers to continue shouting a specific phrase at President Donald Trump during his rallies. The incident occurred when a crowd member at a Trump rally in Mississippi yelled, 'Shove that ballroom up your fat ass!' during Trump's speech, prompting security to remove the individual. Kimmel, during his Tuesday night monologue, expressed hope that this phrase would become a recurring chant at Trump's events, joking that it would be 'a shame' if people started wearing shirts with the phrase. He specifically warned against the phrase being used at Trump's upcoming rallies in Ohio and South Carolina, stating it would be 'beneath us.' The phrase refers to Trump's planned $600 million White House ballroom project, which has faced scrutiny over its escalating costs. item.title: The Hidden Dangers of Sovereign Baby Movements: A Critical Look at Free-Birthing and Government Distrust
item.description: The article explores the growing 'sovereign baby' movement, where parents reject traditional medical systems and government documentation for their children. It highlights the deep distrust of medical institutions, particularly among women of color, who face systemic disparities in maternal care. The piece follows Sarah Ashley Townsend, whose mother refused hospital births and paperwork, leaving her without a birth certificate or Social Security number for most of her life. Townsend recounts the lifelong challenges she faced, including being denied a driver's license and struggling to secure her son's birth certificate due to her own lack of documentation. The article emphasizes the maternal health crisis in the U.S., especially for women of color, while cautioning against the dangers of unassisted births, which have led to infant and parental deaths. item.title: Pokémon Unite to Discontinue Switch Service in March 2027
item.description: Pokémon Unite, the free-to-play MOBA game developed by Tencent Games and published by The Pokémon Company, is set to end its service on the Nintendo Switch in March 2027. This announcement has been met with mixed reactions from the gaming community, with many players expressing disappointment over the game's monetization practices and the lack of alternatives for console players. The game, which launched on July 21, 2021, has faced criticism for its aggressive in-game purchases, including expensive cosmetic items like $40 skins for Pokémon characters. Players have noted that the game's monetization model has been a significant factor in its declining popularity, with many stating that the high costs discouraged regular play. The game's developer, Tencent Games, has been criticized for not providing a sustainable model that balances free-to-play elements with fair pricing. item.title: Chiricahua Becomes America's 64th National Park, Celebrating Unique Geological Formations
item.description: Chiricahua National Monument in southeastern Arizona has been officially designated as America's 64th national park, marking the first new addition to the national park system in six years. Located in the Chiricahua Mountains, the park features a unique landscape of balanced rocks and rhyolite spires that have formed over millions of years. The area, known to the Apache people as 'the land of standing-up rocks,' covers approximately 12,000 acres of canyon country and includes hundreds of pinnacles that can reach up to hundreds of feet in height. The geological formations were created by volcanic activity approximately 27 million years ago, when the Turkey Creek eruption deposited vast amounts of ash that later cooled and fractured into columns. Over time, water erosion and freeze-thaw cycles shaped these columns into the distinctive spires seen today. item.title: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Calls for International Attention on Kashmir, Resource Management, and Energy Infrastructure
item.description: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Azar addressed the Karachi Press Club during a Meet the Press event, emphasizing the need for greater international focus on the region's constitutional status, natural resources, and economic challenges. He expressed concerns about the proposal to grant Gilgit-Baltistan provisional provincial status, stressing that the region's constitutional and political issues must be resolved before any such move. Azar criticized India's 2019 decision to revoke Jammu and Kashmir's special status, arguing that the international community has failed to take meaningful action against Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He also highlighted the mismanagement of Gilgit-Baltistan's mineral resources, alleging that gold worth Rs15 billion is being extracted daily from the region. Azar called for restrictions on transporting raw minerals outside the region to prevent resource depletion. Additionally, he pointed out that high electricity costs, at Rs60 per unit

item.title: Elsa Lanchester's Early Career in 1920s London: Cabaret, Film, and Stage
item.description: Elsa Lanchester, the British actress later famous for her role as the Bride of Frankenstein, began her career in the late 1920s in London's vibrant bohemian scene. Before achieving Hollywood fame, she established herself as a multifaceted performer through cabaret ownership, music hall comedy, and early film roles. In the early 1920s, she co-founded and managed The Cave of Harmony, a popular London nightclub that became a hub for avant-garde artists and intellectuals including Evelyn Waugh, Christopher Isherwood, and Osbert Sitwell. Lanchester gained recognition for her satirical performances, often wearing top hats, tights, and high heels while performing cheeky, socially critical sketches and singing Victorian-era ballads. Her recordings, such as 'Please Sell No More Drink to My Father' (1926), were released on Columbia Records. item.title: Earwax's Dual Properties Offer Insights for Developing Natural Insect Repellents
item.description: Earwax, medically known as cerumen, has long been recognized for its role in ear health, but recent research reveals its unique physical properties could inspire safer insect repellents. Scientists from Georgia Institute of Technology conducted experiments observing how ants interact with earwax, discovering it possesses a paradoxical combination of slipperiness and stickiness. The study, published in the journal Soft Matter, found that earwax's structure—composed of skin flakes held together by a binder—creates a surface that ants struggle to navigate. When ants attempted to climb smooth earwax, they immediately fell due to the material's ability to absorb the moisture from their wet suction cups, preventing attachment. This dual property, known as shear-thinning, allows earwax to thin under physical deformation while maintaining its sticky nature. item.title: SK Hynix predicts memory shortages will continue through 2030 amid AI-driven demand
item.description: SK Hynix, a leading South Korean memory manufacturer, has forecasted that global memory shortages will persist until at least 2030, driven by surging demand from artificial intelligence infrastructure development. The company reported a significant quarterly revenue increase of ₩104.6 trillion ($78.1 billion), a 328 percent year-over-year growth, with operating profit reaching ₩87.68 trillion ($62.8 billion), up 486 percent annually. SK Hynix attributes this success to a 'virtuous cycle' where AI adoption drives increased infrastructure investment, which in turn fuels further AI development. The company noted that supply is not keeping pace with market growth due to technical challenges in leading-edge manufacturing processes and lengthy facility construction timelines. Despite planning to expand production capacity, SK Hynix acknowledged it cannot meet demand quickly enough, with 14 long-term contracts securing over half of its 2027-2028 output. item.title: Religious and racial divides shape Brazil's presidential election dynamics
item.description: Brazil's 2026 presidential election revealed deep political divisions rooted in religious and racial identities, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva securing a narrow victory over Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The election highlighted how religious affiliations, particularly between Catholics and evangelicals, intersect with racial demographics. According to the article, 57% of Brazilians identify as Catholic and 27% as evangelical, reflecting a significant shift from three decades ago when 80% were Catholic. item.title: Los Angeles sues celebrity dog rescue for operating as illegal business
item.description: The Los Angeles city attorney's office has filed a lawsuit against Wagmor Pets, an animal rescue organization once popular among Hollywood celebrities, alleging it operates as an illegal commercial enterprise. item.title: Los Angeles Board Suspends Utility Shutoffs Amid Unusually High Bills
item.description: The Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (DWP) board has suspended residential water and electricity service shutoffs for nonpayment through the end of the year following a period of unusually high utility bills. The board, which does not have the authority to forgive the charges, encouraged residents to enroll in programs that could help alleviate rising costs. The move comes as complaints about unexpectedly high bills have spread widely on social media, with residents describing bills as 'outrageous,' 'insane,' and 'extremely crazy.' During the most recent bimonthly billing period, DWP customers saw a 15% to 20% median increase in electricity use compared to the same period last year, with unusual weather conditions, including a tripling of extreme heat warning days from five in 2025 to 15 in 2026, contributing to the spike. Floris and Benavides, who previously oversaw investigations into foreign influence efforts tied to Donald Trump's campaign, are accused of lying to House investigators in 2023 about their involvement in probes related to Hunter Biden's laptop. item.title: North Carolina Voters Face Ballot Rejection Crisis Due to GOP-Imposed Sealing Rule
item.description: Thousands of voters in North Carolina, a key battleground state for the 2026 midterms, are encountering significant issues with their mail-in ballots due to a new Republican-imposed requirement that the inner ballot envelope must be completely sealed inside the outer envelope. According to data compiled by Common Cause North Carolina from statewide election data through October 24, 2026, nearly 6 percent of mail ballots counted so far have been flagged with problems, totaling 3,672 ballots still in jeopardy. Another 742 voters have already corrected their ballots, but approximately two-thirds of all problematic ballots were spoiled outright, meaning they cannot be repaired with a simple attestation form.
